questions.explanation: With the definitions used here, \(S = 1/(1+L)\) multiplies a disturbance added at the output. Reference to output is the complementary sensitivity \(T\). Reference to the control signal is the control sensitivity, not \(S\).

questions.prompt: A loop has loop gain \(L = 8\). The sensitivity \(S = 1/(1+L)\) is
questions.explanation: \(S = 1/(1+8) = 1/9 = 0.111\). The complementary sensitivity \(T = 8/9\) is one minus \(S\). The loop gain 8 is not the sensitivity.

questions.prompt: Same loop, \(L = 8\). The complementary sensitivity \(T\) is
questions.explanation: \(T = L/(1+L) = 8/9 = 0.889\). Check: \(T + S = 8/9 + 1/9 = 1\). The sensitivity 0.111 is not the complementary sensitivity.

questions.prompt: For \(S = 1/(1+L)\) and \(T = L/(1+L)\), the identity \(S + T = 1\) holds
questions.explanation: Adding the definitions gives \(1/(1+L) + L/(1+L) = 1\) wherever \(L\) is defined, stable or not. Unity feedback is a separate fact: it makes \(T\) equal the reference-to-output map. A non-unity sensor changes that map, not this algebra. The identity is not limited to DC.

questions.explanation: When \(|L| \gg 1\), \(S \approx 1/L \to 0\) and \(T \approx L/L = 1\). This is the low-frequency region for most loops. At high frequency where \(|L| \ll 1\), \(S \approx 1\) and \(T \approx L \to 0\).

questions.prompt: A design limits the peak sensitivity \(M_s = \max |S(j\omega)|\) to 2. The minimum distance from the Nyquist curve to \(-1\) is
questions.explanation: The peak sensitivity is the reciprocal of the closest approach to \(-1\). If \(M_s = 2\), the curve comes within \(1/2 = 0.5\) of the critical point. A larger \(M_s\) means the curve comes closer to instability.

questions.explanation: For a stable plant with at least one right-half plane zero or time delay, the area under \(\ln|S|\) is fixed. Pushing \(|S|\) down at low frequency pushes it up at high frequency. There is no free lunch in sensitivity.

questions.prompt: A loop has \(L(0) = 20\). The steady-state error to a unit step reference is
questions.explanation: At DC, \(S(0) = 1/(1+20) = 1/21 = 0.048\). The error is \(S \cdot r = 0.048 \times 1\). The complementary sensitivity \(20/21\) is what the output reaches.

questions.prompt: At the phase crossover, \(|L| = 0.1\). The gain margin in dB is
questions.explanation: Gain margin is read where the phase is \(-180^\circ\), not at the gain crossover where \(|L| = 1\). Here \(|L| = 0.1\), so the gain can increase by a factor of 10 before that crossing reaches \(-1\). In decibels that factor is \(20\log_{10}(10) = 20\).

questions.prompt: The Gang of Four in feedback analysis consists of
questions.explanation: The Gang of Four are the four closed-loop transfer functions: \(S\) (sensitivity), \(T\) (complementary sensitivity), \(PS\) (output to disturbance), and \(CS\) (control sensitivity). They fully characterize the closed-loop behavior.

questions.prompt: A specification requires \(|S(j\omega)| < 0.1\) at \(\omega = 0.1\) rad/s. The minimum \(|L(j0.1)|\) is
questions.explanation: From \(|S| = 1/|1+L| < 0.1\), we need \(|1+L| > 10\), so approximately \(|L| > 9\). The exact bound depends on the phase of \(L\), but for real \(L > 0\), \(L > 9\) suffices.
